**Pietro Sala** is an applied economist working on agricultural, water and resource
economics. He is a PhD candidate (expected April 2027) and research associate at the
Chair of Agricultural Production and Resource Economics, TUM School of Management,
Technical University of Munich.

His research measures how efficiently farms and food systems use natural resources, and how
to separate weather-driven losses from managerial shortfalls. Methodologically he works with
stochastic frontier analysis, productivity and eco-efficiency measurement, panel
econometrics and causal machine learning (double/debiased ML, LASSO). He has worked on two
EU research projects: PONDERFUL (ponds as nature-based solutions) and RETOUCH NEXUS (water
governance and the water–energy–food–ecosystems nexus), and coordinates the chair's research
partnerships in Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Cambodia).

## Selected publications

- Sala, P. et al. (2025). Evaluating ponds as nature-based solutions: Effectiveness and eco-efficiency. *Journal of Environmental Management* 393, 126933. [doi:10.1016/j.jenvman.2025.126933](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2025.126933)
- Bremer et al. (2026). Bridging the nexus: Policy and welfare dimensions in hydro-economic models. *Water Resources Management* 40, 501. [doi:10.1007/s11269-026-04848-0](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11269-026-04848-0)
- Dinov et al. (2026). Environmental Kuznets Curve applications for water pollution in the EU. *Journal of Environmental Management* 398, 127942. [doi:10.1016/j.jenvman.2025.127942](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2025.127942)
- Blicharska et al. (2026). Challenges for assessing and implementing nature-based solutions at landscape scale. *Hydrobiologia*. [doi:10.1007/s10750-026-06212-0](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10750-026-06212-0)
- Twohig et al. (2026). Economic implications of water scarcity in the WEFE nexus: the Upper Main basin. SSRN 7307240.
